title: Grundlagen & Wärmetransport

learn.h: Conduction (the single most important formula in the course)
items: Fourier's Law: $\dot q=-\lambda\,\delta T/\delta n$ — derive/recognize it in both the flux form and the homogeneous-body form
Know $\lambda$'s units [W/(m·K)] and what it physically represents
Be able to compute $\Delta Q/\Delta t = \lambda A (T_1-T_2)/l$ for a simple slab
$\Phi_{CV}=h\cdot A\cdot(\theta_f-\theta_s)$ — know $h$ differs for free vs. forced convection in air

learn.h: Radiation trio (know cold — resurfaces via Globethermometer in M10, solar radiation in M11)
items: Stefan-Boltzmann: $M_s=\sigma T^4$, $\sigma=5.6697\times10^{-8}$ W/(m²K⁴)
Wien's displacement law: $\lambda_{max}=2896\times10^{-6}\text{K·m}/T$
Kirchhoff's law: $\varepsilon=\alpha$; real-body radiation $M=\varepsilon\sigma T^4$
Energy balance: $\rho+\alpha+\tau=1$ (reflectance + absorptance + transmittance)
The four Hauptsätze (just recognize them)
Carnot efficiency $\eta=(T_2-T_1)/T_2$ (both temperatures in Kelvin)
Joule/Watt/kWh relationships, enthalpy/entropy at a conceptual level

learn.h: Method skills — costs you points silently if skipped
items: SI base units (2019 redefinition), SI prefixes
Scientific notation
Significant figures: multiplication/division rule vs. addition/subtraction rule — don't conflate them
Basic measurement-error vocabulary
Bauphysik vs. Tragwerkslehre vs. Baustoffkunde
PMV/PPD (name-drop only here, developed in M09 Thermischer Komfort)
SBS vs. BRI
Wärmebrücke (defined here, developed in M03 Wärmebrücken, Dämmung & Speichermasse)
Nachhaltigkeit / Effizienz / Effektivität / Suffizienz (developed further in M12 Bauökologie & OI3-Index)

risk: Every numeric answer in the exam is a chance to lose points on units, significant figures, or scientific notation — this isn't optional background, it's graded on every later Rechenbeispiel.

title: Stationäre U-Werte (Homogene Bauteile)

learn.h: The U-value formula chain — know cold, both directions
items: $R=d/\lambda$ (single layer) → $R=\sum d_k/\lambda_k$ (multi-layer)
$R_T=R_{si}+\sum R+R_{se}$
$\dot q=U(\theta_i-\theta_e)$
Back-solve: given a target U-value, find the required insulation thickness or λ
Recursive method: $\theta_n=\theta_{n-1}-\dot q\cdot R_n$
Both the numeric and graphical (Formblatt) approaches
Understand this is the direct groundwork for condensation-risk assessment (M05, M06)
ruhend vs. schwach belüftet vs. stark belüftet
**Hinterlüftung is excluded from the R-sum; Installationsebene is included** — lecturer explicitly said this is graded
$U_m=\sum A_iU_i/\sum A_i$ — practice not missing any component's area
Distinguish "% of original" vs. "% reduction" framing in retrofit questions
Headline values: Wand 0.35, Fenster 1.4/1.7, Dach 0.20, Boden 0.40 — unchanged since 2007
Default-Werte hierarchy for existing buildings: plan data > analogy/inspection > Default-Werte (last resort only)

learn.h: Lecturer-flagged favorite questions — rehearse the exact answers
items: Does U depend on area or ΔT? → **No**
Is U = 10 W/m²K possible? → **No**, physical maximum ≈ 5.883
What's the series/parallel-circuit analogy for a building envelope?
Is higher or lower charakteristische Länge better?

risk:
**Two explicit trap questions**
"Does U depend on A or ΔT?" (no) and "Is U=10 W/m²K possible?" (no — physical max ≈5.883) are named lecturer favorites. Answer both from memory, not derivation, under time pressure.

title: Wärmebrücken, Dämmung & Speichermasse

learn.h: Wärmebrücken fundamentals — the conceptual heart of this module
items: Why **"wärmebrückenfrei" is wrong**; the correct term is **"wärmebrückenminimiert"**
Why **"Kältebrücke" is physically wrong** — explicitly the lecturer's own favorite question to ask; be able to give the 2nd-law-of-thermodynamics justification in writing
$f_{Rsi}$ thresholds: 0.71 = mould risk, 0.69 = condensation risk
$\psi$ (linear) and $\chi$ (point) thermal-bridge coefficients, and their sign pitfalls
Diagnostics: thermography, simulation
Minimization strategies
The oberer/unterer Grenzwert (upper/lower bound) method — conceptually, and able to critique it (lecturer is openly skeptical)
Note: only simple cases are hand-calculated on the exam; Formelsammlung is provided
$U_w=\dfrac{\sum A_gU_g+\sum A_fU_f+\sum l_g\Psi_g}{A_f+A_g}$
Know what each term represents: glazing, frame, edge-seal linear loss
$S=c\rho$ (Wärmespeicherzahl), $C=cm$ (Wärmekapazität), $C_m=cM$ (molare Wärmekapazität) — know the mass/volume/amount-of-substance distinction
Amplitude damping & phase shift (time-lag) — conceptual; mud-brick vs. concrete as memory hook
λ-value ranges, and 2–3 distinguishing facts per material: MW, EPS, XPS, Schaumglas, Holzfasern, Stroh, Kork, Hanf, Zellulose, Aerogel, Vakuumpaneele
Not required to memorize every table value — recognize materials by characteristic properties
Pont & Mahdavi (2017) — explicitly quizzed in the official question bank: know the research question, method, and conclusion (2D approximation of 3D thermal bridges can mislead)

risk:
**Named favorites, verbatim**
"Kältebrücke" is explicitly called the lecturer's own favorite question. "Wärmebrückenfrei" being wrong is tested twice in the course (here and again in M13's repetitorium). Free points if the 2nd-law justification is written cleanly.

title: Instationäres Wärmeverhalten

items: Thermal equilibrium (ΔT=0, $\dot Q$=0) vs. stationär (ΔT constant) vs. instationär (both non-constant)
Conceptual anchor: why doesn't the daily outdoor temperature swing reach the inside surface?

learn.h: Thermal diffusivity — the conceptual core of this module
items: $a=\lambda/(\rho c)$
The Holz/Beton/Polystyrol counter-intuitive result: Polystyrol has the *lowest* λ but the *fastest* apparent temperature response, because $\rho c$ is so small
Understand: λ alone cannot explain non-stationary behaviour — always need $\rho c$ too

learn.h: Contact temperature — drilled twice in the source lecture
items: Wärmeeindringkoeffizient $b=\sqrt{\lambda\rho c}$
$\theta_c=(b_1\theta_1+b_2\theta_2)/(b_1+b_2)$
Know: a *high*-$b$ material (metal) feels *colder* to the touch than a *low*-$b$ material (wood) at the **same** temperature — this is the formula-backed version of M01's sauna-bench observation

learn.h: Dynamic room heat balance & neutral temperature
items: The reduced ODE: $\theta_i(t)+\tau\cdot d\theta_i/dt=\theta_e(t)+\gamma\cdot E_{ST}(t)$

Key distinction: $\tau$ (time constant) affects only the **amplitude** of the swing; $\gamma$ (gain/loss ratio) affects **both** average level and amplitude — this is the single most likely exam-question source in this module
Why two-sided ventilation + thermal mass beats one-sided (Atrium/Kamineffekt)
Caveat: thermal mass only helps if thermally *accessible* (not hidden behind a suspended ceiling)
Multizonal, hourly, weather-file-driven simulation basics
What shading vs. night ventilation each buy you (worked example: 10%→70%→100% comfort-band hours)

risk: The $\tau$-vs-$\gamma$ distinction (amplitude-only vs. amplitude-and-level) is the conceptual core the lecturer built the whole session around — expect a question that tests whether you actually understand the difference, not just the symbols.

title: Feuchtigkeit & Hygrische Grundlagen

learn.h: Atmosphere & gas laws — the physics underneath everything else here
items: Dry-air composition; Dampf as ideales Gas
Boyle-Mariotte ($pV=$const), Gay-Lussac/Charles ($V/T=$const), Amontons ($p/T=$const)
Stoffmenge $n=m/M$; allgemeine Zustandsgleichung $pV=mRT$
Dalton's law / Partialdruck: $p_{Gesamt}=\sum p_i$
$x$/$c$/$p$ units for humidity content
Magnus formula for saturation pressure: $p_S=a(b+\vartheta/100°C)^n$ — **it's a power law, not linear**
Relative Luftfeuchtigkeit: $\varphi=x/x_s=c/c_s=p/p_s$
Work the Badezimmer worked example end to end
Be able to read $\theta$, $\varphi$, $x$, $p_D$, $\rho$, $h$ off a point (no memorization of values needed)
Trace the five HVAC state-change paths: Mischen, Erwärmung, Kühlung, Befeuchtung, Wärmerückgewinnung
$\dot m=\dot V\rho$, $\dot V=vA$
Raumluftfeuchte-Gleichgewicht formula
The density lookup step via the Mollier diagram

learn.h: Material moisture & vapor diffusion — core note
items: Wassergehalt $u$; Übersättigungs-/Kapillar-/Sorptionsbereich; Sorptionsisothermen
Fick's law and its explicit analogy to Fourier's law: $\dot m=-D\Delta c/\Delta x$
**µ-value / $s_d$-value** — flagged as a favorite exam question: $\dot m=\Delta p/(1.5\times10^6\cdot\mu\cdot s)$, $s_d=\mu\cdot s$

learn.h: Surface condensation & mould risk — core note, *"so gut wie bei jeder Prüfung"*
items: Sättigungstemperatur closed form: $\theta_S=\varphi^{1/8}(110+\theta_L)-110$
Be able to solve for whichever of $\theta_{si}$, $\varphi$, $\theta_S$, or $U$ is missing, given the others
Tie-back: how this connects to M03's $f_{Rsi}$ thresholds (0.71/0.69) — VO8 explains *why* those numbers are what they are
Schimmelpilz growth conditions (5–6 named factors) — and that colour is **not** diagnostic

risk:
**"So gut wie bei jeder Prüfung"**
The lecturer's own words for the surface-condensation worked example. Practice solving it for all four unknowns (not just $\theta_{si}$) until it's automatic.

title: Glaser-Verfahren & Tauwasserschutz

items: M02's layer-temperature recursion — the Glaser-Formblatt *is* that same Formblatt with extra columns
M05's µ-value/$s_d$-value and Magnus/saturation-pressure formulas — reused wholesale here

learn.h: The construction procedure itself — the core skill
items: Axis setup: Y = Wasserdampfdruck, X = cumulative µ·d
Keep a **consistent scale** — rescaling mid-axis is the named favorite mistake
Plot the linear Partialdrucklinie
Plot the polygon Sättigungsdampfdruck-Zug (saturation pressure depends only on temperature at each layer boundary, from the Formblatt)
Read off whether/where the two lines cross → condensation criterion: condensate wherever saturation-pressure polygon ≤ partial-pressure line
Practice the **Kein-Kondensat** case and the **Kondensatanfall** case (including the multi-crossing variant)

learn.h: Two layer-placement rules — let you predict the outcome without drawing
items: Layer with the largest temperature drop (insulation) → as far **outside** as possible
Layer with the largest µ·d-value (vapor barrier/retarder) → as far **inside** as possible
Practice applying these rules directly to a cross-section, no diagram, as a speed check

learn.h: U-value says nothing about Bauteilkondensat — flagged favorite theory question
items: Identical U-value, reversed layer order (Außendämmung vs. Innendämmung) → completely different Glaser outcome — be able to explain why in words
Tauperiode mass flow: $\dot m_T=\dot m_e-\dot m_a$, condensate $G_K=1440\dot m_T$
Trockenperiode mass flow: $\dot m_A=\dot m_{a1}+\dot m_{a2}$, drying $G_A=2160\dot m_A$
$G_A/G_K>1$ = complete drying-out — acceptable for mineral Bauteile, **never** acceptable for Holzkonstruktionen (which must show zero condensate to begin with)
Work the Seileck (funicular-line) method for reading off Tauperiode/Trockenperiode graphically
Placement principle: as far inside as possible, before any layer with a strong temperature drop
Graphical effect: a high-$s_d$ layer stretches the saturation-pressure polygon far right, pulling it clear of the partial-pressure line
Steady-state only — no Speichereffekte / hygroskopische Pufferung
No Wärmebrücken-Berücksichtigung
Inhomogeneous components need every cross-section checked separately
$R_{si}$ choice (0.13 vs. 0.25) changes the outcome
Same U-Wert-Formblatt from M02/M03, now with all columns filled — practice a full pass, not just the Glaser-specific columns
Work through the real exam-derived example

risk:
**Guaranteed exam item**
Not "likely" — the lecturer states directly that a Glaser diagram appears on every exam, worth 7 of ~30–31 points. See M13 for the full worked repetitorium example and step-by-step construction walkthrough used there.

title: Gebäude-Energiebilanz (Heizwärmebedarf)

learn.h: The master energy balance formula — know every term
items: $Q_H=[\Phi_T+\Phi_V-\eta(\Phi_S+\Phi_I)]\Delta t$
What each term physically represents, and the unit conversion W → J via $\Delta t$
$\Phi_T=AU\Delta\theta$ (component level)
Building level: $H_T=\sum A_iU_i\,(+\sum L_j\Psi_j+\sum z_k\chi_k)$ — this is M02/M03's U-value and ψ/χ machinery scaled to a whole building
$\Phi_V=\frac{n}{3600}Vc_a\rho_a\Delta\theta$, simplified $H_V\approx0.34nV$
Why lüften is necessary despite the energy cost (air quality, moisture, comfort)
Free vs. mechanical ventilation, Wärmerückgewinnung
$\Phi_S=AF_rgE_{sT}$ — Rahmenanteil, G-Wert/SHGC, Strahlungssumme
**Named favorite calculation trap** (flagged again in VO15): multiply radiation sums by the relevant surface orientation **first**, only then sum across surfaces/months — not the reverse
People (~100–120 W/Person), devices, lighting — simple but real exam calculation

learn.h: Ausnutzungsgrad $\eta_h$ & Zeitkonstante $\tau$ — closes the loop opened by M04
items: Conceptually: why gains aren't 100% usable (thermal inertia, timing mismatch)
$\gamma_h=(\Phi_S+\Phi_I)/(\Phi_T+\Phi_V)$; $\gamma_h=0$ if $\Phi_T+\Phi_V<0$
$\eta_h=(1-\gamma_h^a)/(1-\gamma_h^{a+1})$, $a=a_0+\tau/\tau_0$
$\tau=C/(H_T+H_V)$ — reuses M03's thermal-mass concepts at building/zone scale (only ~10 cm of wall depth counts as accessible storage)
Full EN ISO 13790 formula is more likely tested as "know it exists / plug into it" than derived from scratch

learn.h: Three calculation types — know when each applies
items: Heizlast (system sizing, Referenztemperatur)
Jährlicher Heizwärmebedarf (Energieausweis, typisches Jahr)
Transientes Verfahren (dynamic simulation, hourly weather data)
Konditioniertes Bruttovolumen (measured via Außenabmessungen — same convention as M02's $U_m$), Bezugsfläche, Gebäudehüllfläche
Kompaktheit $C=V/A_T$ — Kugel > Kubus > everything else; row houses beat detached houses because party walls are adiabatic (worked example: freestanding cube $C=1.32$ vs. mid-terrace cube $C=1.98$)
Luftdichtigkeit / Blower-Door: $Q=C\Delta p^m$, the $n_{50}$ value — ventilation losses can reach **~60% of total losses** in a well-insulated (Passivhaus-grade) building
Grundrissplanung, Verglasung/Orientierung, Wärmedämmung, Wärmespeicherkapazität as a rote-recall "name 3 measures to reduce X" structure
Heizgradtage: $Q_T=U_mA_T\cdot HGT\cdot24\cdot3600$; $Q_V=0.34nV\cdot HGT\cdot24\cdot3600$ (needs M08's HGT figure)
Real-building calibration points: Minergie-P Schule (9.8 kWh/m²a), Passivhaus benchmark (~50 kWh/m²a new construction), Gründerzeit-Altbau (~200 kWh/m²a)
Certification systems by name: LEED, BREEAM, DGNB, Minergie, ÖGNB/ÖGNI, klima:aktiv
1°C-lower-heating nationwide → ≈ −6% national energy use
Well-insulated envelope → surface temperature ≈ air temperature

risk:
**Named calculation trap**
Solar-gain radiation sums must be multiplied by orientation *before* summing across surfaces — VO15's repetitorium explicitly calls this out as the popular mistake.

title: Klima- & Standortanalyse

learn.h: Heizgradtage/Heiztage — the one real calculation topic here
items: Heizgrenze concept: **12°C, not 20°C** — because of free internal/solar gains
$HT=\sum\Delta t(\bar\theta_e)$ for days where $\theta_e<12°C$
$HGT_{20/12}=\sum(20-\bar\theta_e)$, summed over days where $\theta_e<12°C$
Know this feeds directly into M07's simplified $Q_T$/$Q_V$ method
Makroklima vs. Mikroklima — clean definition question
Temperature, humidity, solar radiation (Globalstrahlung), wind as the building blocks
Köppen-Geiger 5 climate zones (A–E) — names and rough global distribution
IPCC scenarios, at a conceptual level
Urban Heat Island mechanism: heat trapped in urban mass, anthropogenic heat, reduced ventilation, dark surfaces — more pronounced at night and under weak wind
The Cooling Singapore UHI research project as a memory hook
UTCI's 4 input variables (conceptual only, not the formula) — this is only introduced here; the full structure comes in M10
Categorization: openings/glazing, envelope, thermal mass (reuses M03's thermal-mass concepts as a design strategy)
Psychrometric chart / Givoni diagram zones: CZ, NV, HM, HMV, EC
Caveat: only valid for low-internal-gain residential/office buildings

learn.h: Building in the four climate zones — historical & modern comparison table
items: Kalt / gemäßigt / arid / tropisch — Grundprinzipien per zone
Case-study memory hooks: Iglu, Sisimiut, courtyard houses, Sumatra stilt houses

risk: The Heizgrenze is 12°C, not 20°C — a clean trap if you reason from "room temperature" intuition instead of the free-gains logic.

title: Thermischer Komfort

items: Homöotherm regulation; Vasodilatation vs. Vasokonstriktion; Hypothalamus as control center
37°C core-temperature target and the danger table
VO12's fresh framing: Homöostase, Regulierer vs. Konformer, negative vs. positive Rückkopplung (Eis-Albedo = positive-feedback example), endotherm/homoiotherm vs. ektotherm/poikilotherm

learn.h: Conditions for comfort & the comfort equation
items: Thermal neutrality + energy balance as the two conditions
$\Delta S=M-W-E_v\pm R_d\pm C_d\pm C_v$
$M=Q_{sk}+Q_{res}+S+W$
Stoffwechselrate (Met): 1 met = 58 W/m² sitting person; DuBois body-surface formula $A_{Du}=0.202\,W^{0.425}H^{0.725}$
Bekleidung (Clo): 1 clo = 0.155 m²K/W; typical values (Business-Anzug ≈1 clo, Sommerkleidung ≈0.5 clo)
6 input factors: Met, Clo, Lufttemperatur, Strahlungstemperatur, Luftgeschwindigkeit, Wasserdampfdruck
7-point Wärmeempfindensskala, and PMV↔PPD relationship (even PMV=0 still gives 5% PPD)
**The full PMV formula itself is explicitly excluded from the exam** — only the concept and reading a calculator output
Mittlere Strahlungstemperatur: $\bar\theta_r=\sum A_i\theta_{s,i}/A_{tot}$
Full: $\theta_0=(h_c\theta_a+h_r\bar\theta_r)/(h_c+h_r)$; simplified: $\theta_0\approx(\theta_a+\bar\theta_r)/2$
Compensation logic: low air temp can be offset by high mrt and vice versa, within ±3–8°C
Redo the 22/22°C → 18°C mrt → 26°C worked example from memory
Why it exists: Fanger's bands were too narrow for naturally ventilated buildings
Applies **only to natürlich belüftete** buildings, never klimatisiert/HVAC
VO6 constants: $T_{comfort}=0.31\,T_{rm}+17.8$
**VO12 constants — deliberately different, not an error**: $\theta_c=0.33\,\theta_{rm}+18.8$ — know both and which VO each comes from
Winter: 19–24°C (1 clo / 1.2 met); Sommer: 23.5–26.5°C (0.5 clo / 1.2 met)
Local-discomfort thresholds: 3K head/foot, 4K/10K/13K/20K radiant asymmetry, air speed <0.15/<0.2 m/s
Four causes: Zugluft, Strahlungsasymmetrie, vertikale Lufttemperaturdifferenz, Fußkomfort
Why warme Decken/kalte Wände are worse than the reverse → design implication: Fußbodenheizung + Deckenkühlung, not the other way around

risk:
**The VO6/VO12 constant discrepancy is deliberate — don't "correct" it**
$0.31/17.8$ (VO6) vs. $0.33/18.8$ (VO12) is a genuine contradiction left in the course material on purpose. If asked which to use, cite the source rather than picking one as "the right answer."

title: Sensorik, IAQ & Thermische Indizes

learn.h: Sensor types — lecturer-flagged favorite question pairs
items: Temperature: Ausdehnungs-/Quecksilberthermometer vs. PTC vs. NTC vs. HNTC resistance sensors
Air speed: Schalenkreuz-/Flügelradanemometer vs. Hitzdrahtanemometer
Humidity: Haarhygrometer vs. kapazitiv vs. Psychrometer
Mechanical vs. electronic measurement, generally
Mittlere Strahlungstemperatur, Flächen-Methode: $\bar\theta_r=\sum A_i\theta_{s,i}/A_{tot}$ (reused from M09) plus the Raumwinkel/Steradiant variant

Globethermometer: what it actually measures (a blend of air and radiant temperature, needs settling time), and the back-calculation formula: $\theta_R=\sqrt[4]{(\theta_G+273)^4+2.5\times10^8(\theta_G-\theta_L)v^{0.6}}-273$ — first VO to explain a formula that was sitting unexplained in the Formelsammlung since the start of the course
Simplified VO12 form: $\theta_{OP}=(\theta_L+\theta_U)/2$ — compare against M09's $\theta_0\approx(\theta_a+\bar\theta_r)/2$
Know that `PMVcalc_v2` and the CBE Thermal Comfort Tool exist and what they're used for (a live-demo calculator, not hand computation)

**The wet/dry heat-loss-vs-operative-temperature graph** — *"Ich gebe diese Abbildung sehr gerne bei der Prüfung"*: be able to read off which fraction is trocken (sensible) vs. feucht (latent) heat loss at a given activity level and temperature
Emission vs. Immission
MAK vs. MIK — explicitly flagged **"sehr beliebte Prüfungsfrage"**: MIK ≈ 1/20 of MAK
Pettenkofer's 1000 ppm CO2 recommendation
Read the Pettenkofer-Diagramm (fresh-air-per-person vs. CO2-ppm, log-log) for a worked example
CO2-Sensorik basics (Infrarotspektroskopie)

learn.h: Thermal indices — full structure, first time explained
items: UTCI: needs 4 inputs (Lufttemperatur 2m, Taupunkt/rel. Feuchte 2m, Windgeschwindigkeit 10m, mittlere Strahlungstemperatur); **not** a real thermometer reading; **is dynamic/time-dependent** — stress-category bands (e.g. 26–32°C = moderate heat stress)
PET, GT, SET* — know these are **stationary** (steady-state), indoor-referenced models, unlike UTCI
Not required to reproduce any of the underlying equations — concepts only, sourced from VDI 3787 Blatt 2 (Pflichtliteratur)

risk:
**Two named favorites in this module**
Sensor-type pairs (PTC/NTC/HNTC etc.) and the MAK/MIK ratio are both explicitly called out as popular exam questions — rehearse both as quick-recall facts, not derivations.

title: Sommerliche Überwärmung

items: Diagram-reading procedure for $E_{S,H}$ (Trübungsfaktor $T$, Luftdruckverhältnis $p/p_0$, Sonnenhöhe $h$)
$E_H=\tfrac{1}{3}[E_0\sin h-E_{S,H}]$
$E_{Glob}=E_{S,H}+E_H$
These formulas already sat in the Formelsammlung since M08 — this is where they're actually drilled
Klima vs. Wetter — clean definition question, plus the "Trump'sche Falle" framing (weather ≠ climate as a rhetorical trap)
Strahlungsbilanzen: kurzwellig $Q_k=G-R=D+H-R=(1-a)G$; langwellig $Q_l=A_E=A_O-A_G$; gesamt $Q=Q_k-Q_l$ — concepts and influencing factors, no numeric examples
Radiative Forcing (conceptual)
Austria's 7 Klimaregionen
Sonnenhöhe, Deklination, reading a Sonnenbahndiagramm, Horizontüberhöhung

learn.h: ÖNORM B8110-3 & OIB-RL6 — the normative core
items: Immissionsfläche concept
Operative Temperatur im Sommerfall as a **hard limit**, not a comfort target (contrast with M09's comfort-band usage)
OIB 4.9.1a limit formula: $\theta_{op}\leq\tfrac{1}{3}T_{NAT,13}+21.8°C$
The 6–22h / 22–6h Fenster-Randbedingung
Simulation tools by name: TheSim3d, Archiphysik

learn.h: Climate change & UHI — three definitions, don't conflate
items: Tropennacht (night temperature stays above 20°C)
Kysely-Tage (heat-period definition)
Hitzewelle (several slightly different threshold definitions depending on source)
Wiener Hitzekarte as a concrete reference
Lechner Design Strategies
Fixed vs. movable shading typologies, by orientation: Süd (overhangs) vs. Ost/West (fins)

learn.h: Solar gains, glazing, thermal mass (repetition, new annual-sum form)
items: Annual-sum solar gain: $Q_S=\sum_j[I_j\times A_{g,j}\times f_{s,j}\times g_{w,j}]$ — the annual-sum sibling of M07's instantaneous $\Phi_S=AF_rgE_{sT}$
**Named favorite question**: HSG- vs. LSG-Verglasung
Low-E, Vakuumglas — links to M03's window-U-value research
Thermal mass: direct repetition of M03 — no new formulas, just the summer-case framing

risk:
**Three near-identical-sounding definitions**
Tropennacht, Kysely-Tage, and Hitzewelle each use a different threshold logic — a prime multiple-choice trap if studied together without keeping the distinguishing criterion for each explicit.

title: Bauökologie & OI3-Index

learn.h: Bauökologie — Grundbegriffe (deliberate repeat of M01's terminology, with more depth)
items: Ökologie as a concept
Nachhaltigkeit: Carlowitz (1713), Brundtland (1987)
**Starke vs. schwache Nachhaltigkeit** — a definition distinction frequently used as a multiple-choice trap
Resilienz: technisch / ökologisch / evolutionär — watch the confusion risk with Suffizienz (self-limitation ≠ resilience)
Effizienz vs. Effektivität vs. Suffizienz (2000-Watt-Gesellschaft)
SDGs, Kreislaufwirtschaft, Rebound-/Prebound-Effekt, Anthropozän, Planet Boundaries & Overshoot Day, CO2-Historie
Three sub-indicators: GWP, AP, PECnr (PENRT)
Their linear evaluation functions (apply from the Formelsammlung — not required to memorize):
OI3KON of a component: $OI3_{KON}=\tfrac{1}{3}OI_{PECnr}+\tfrac{1}{3}OI_{GWP}+\tfrac{1}{3}OI_{AP}$
$\Delta OI3$ of a single layer (new formula, not pre-existing in the Formelsammlung)
**Symbol warning**: $x$ here (Latin, OI evaluation-function input) is unrelated to $\chi$ (Chi, M03's point-thermal-bridge coefficient) — don't conflate them
